title: WPSS/809/2016 of Smt. Malti Mahar AND ANOTHER Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No. 809/16, 548/16, 647/16,
648/16, 803/16, 804/16, 805/16
Honíble Rajiv Sharma, J.
Mr. Jayvardhan Kandpal, Advocate
for the petitioners.
Mr. B.P.S. Mer, Brief Holder for the
State.
Mr. Tapan Singh, Advocate for the
private respondents.
All these petitions have been taken
up together and decided by this common
order, since the same involve the common
questions of law and facts. In order to
maintain clarity, the facts of WPSS No. 809
of 2016 are taken into consideration.
The petitioners are aggrieved by the
advertisement dated 15.03.2016, Annexure
No.6, whereby the qualifications, contrary to
the Recruitment and Promotion Rules
framed under Article 309 of the Constitution
of India, has been inserted.
The minimum qualification
prescribed, under U.P. Dept. of Medical
Health & Family Welfare Health Worker &
Health Supervisor (Male & Female) Service
Rules, 1997 for filling up the posts of
Auxiliary Nursing Midwife, is intermediate
with Science Stream. The aforesaid rules
have duly been adopted by the State of
Uttarakhand.
According to the Rules, the candidate
must possess the qualification prescribed
under the Recruitment and Promotion Rules,
framed under Article 309 of the Constitution
of India. The qualification of Intermediate,
with Science stream, has a nexus to the post
of A.N.M. The qualification of Intermediate in
Science stream has been provided taking
into consideration the duties to be
discharged by the A.N.M.
The qualification of Intermediate with
Arts stream has no nexus with the
specialised job of ANM. Thus, the candidates
having intermediate with Science stream,
are, at least, familiar with the subject
whereas, for the students of Arts, it would
altogether be a new subject.
It is brought to the notice of this
Court that the Nursing Council of India has

issued guidelines in 2012-13, whereby the
qualification of Arts has also been
prescribed.
The guidelines, issued by the Nursing
Counsel of India, cannot be in contravention
to the Rules framed under Article 309 of the
Constitution of India.
Objection has also been raised that
the petitioners have participated in the
selection process thus, precluded from
challenging the qualification. The
qualification of Intermediate with Arts is
absolutely illegal. The petitioners cannot be
precluded from challenging the
advertisement dated 15.03.2016.
It is also submitted at bar that the
State Government, has framed new Rules on
26.07.2016.
The advertisement in the present case
is of dated 15.03.2016. Thus, the same
would be governed under the Recruitment
and Promotion Rules, framed in the year
1998 as amended from time to time.
The qualifications, prescribed in the
prospectus, cannot override the specific
recruitment and promotions Rules.
Their Lordships of Hon. Supreme
Court in (1997) 10 SCC 419 in the case of
ëState of Rajasthan v. R. Dayal & othersí
have held that the posts which fell vacant
prior to the amendment of the rules would
be governed by the original rules and not by
the amended rules. Their Lordships, in
paragraph nos.8 and 9, have held as under:
-
ì8. Therefore, it is not in dispute and cannot be
disputed that while selecting officers, minimum requisite
qualifications and experience for promotion specified in the
relevant column, should be taken into consideration against
vacancies existing as on 1st April of the year of selection.
But since the Rules came to be amended and the
amendment became effective with immediate effect and
clause (11-B) of Rule 24-A indicates that options have been
given to the Government or the appointing Authority, as the
case may be, to revise the select list as existing as per the
law as on the date of the appointment or as may be directed
by a competent court, selection is required to be made by the
concerned DPC. An appointment made, after selection as per
the procedure, to the vacancies existing prior to the
amendment, is valid. But the question is whether selection
would be made, in the case of appointment to the vacancies
which admittedly arose after the amendment of the Rules
came into force, according to the amended Rules or in terms

of Rule 9 read with Rules 23 and 24-A, as mentioned
hereinbefore. This Court has considered the similar question
in para 9 of the judgment above-cited. This Court has
specifically laid that the vacancies which occurred prior to
the amendment of the Rules would be governed by the
original Rules and not by the amended Rules. Accordingly,
this Court had held that the posts which fell vacant prior to
the amendment of the Rules would be governed by the
original Rules and not the amended Rules. As a necessary
corollary, the vacancies that arose subsequent to the
amendment of the Rules are required to be filled in in
accordance with the law existing as on the date when the
vacancies arose. Undoubtedly, the selection came to be made
prior to the amendment of the Rules in accordance with law
then existing since the anticipated vacancies also must have
been taken into consideration in the light of Rule 9 of the
Rules. But after the amended Rules came into force,
necessarily the amended Rules would be required to be
applied for and given effect to. But, unfortunately, that has
not been done in the present case. The two courses are open
to the Government or the appointing authority, viz., either to
make temporary promotions for the ensuing financial year
until the DPC meets or in exercise of the power under Rule
24-A(11-B), they can revise the panel already prepared in
accordance with the Rules and make appointments in
accordance therewith.
9. It is contended by Shri Das that one of the persons,
namely, H.L. Meena was appointed against a carried-forward
post as per the existing Rules and, therefore, his appointment
cannot be challenged. We find it difficult to give acceptance to
the contention. Even a carried-forward vacancy is required to be
considered in accordance with the law existing unless suitable
relaxation is made by the Government. As on that date, when the
appointment came to be made, the selection was required to be
made on the basis of the Rules as existing on the date the
vacancy arose. Since, admittedly, that has not been done, the
appointment of Shri Bhatnagar and H.L. Meena must be treated
to be only temporary appointments pending consideration of the
claims of all the eligible persons belonging to General and
Reserved quota separately as per Rules."
Accordingly, the writ petition is
allowed. The qualification of Intermediate in
Arts is declared illegal. The respondents are
directed to confine the selection process only
to the Intermediate with Science and to do
the needful in accordance with law.
It is made clear by way of abundant
precaution that this judgment is qua the
advertisement dated 15.03.2016 only.
Intervention Application No. 3082 of
2017, being bereft of any merit, is hereby
dismissed.
Pending application, if any, stands
disposed of accordingly.
Let copy of this order be kept in all
the connected matters.
An Ad
